title: Soft-failure scoring + calibration feedback loop for FP8/INT8 structured outputs
creator: Marina Ortiz
description: Problem statement: After applying asymmetric FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles we observe intermittent violations of function-call JSON contracts (missing fields, minor datatype drift, and out-of-range enumerations) that do not always merit a full rollback. Goal: build a soft-failure scoring system plus an automated calibration-feedback loop that quantifies structured-output degradation, proposes targeted calibration updates, and drives canary rollouts with risk-aware thresholds. Deliverables: 1) per-field probabilistic adherence score and composite schema-health metric; 2) calibration suggestion engine that ties scoring signals to calibration knobs (scale tables, per-layer quant profiles, per-batch dynamic rescale); 3) CI harness that runs golden prompt suite across quant profiles and emits actionable failures; 4) runbook and automated canary policy that triggers calibration candidate jobs and optionally pauses rollouts when composite score drops below threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Schema-adherence score computed per inference that decomposes into field-level probabilities and a 0..1 composite health metric
CI harness executes canonical function-call prompt set across fp8/int8/float baselines and records per-prompt delta in composite health

Calibration suggestion engine outputs ranked list of 1-3 concrete changes (eg. increase activation scale for layer 7; enable per-channel symmetric quant for KV cache) with estimated uplift and risk score
Canary automation will halt model rollout if composite health < 0.86 for 1k requests or if field-failure rate has increased by >200% vs baseline
Dashboard exposes per-route trends, top failing prompts, and links to failing example payloads for debugging
End-to-end test: apply suggested calibration change in staging quant pipeline and show composite health improvement >= 5% on canonical prompt set
tasks: Design per-field probabilistic schema scorer (team design doc: confluence/redwood/quant-schema-scorer)
Instrument runtime to emit structured-output traces with field-level metadata and token provenance
Implement offline scorer module and simple moving-window aggregator for composite metric
Build calibration suggestion heuristics mapping score deltas to quant tuning actions
Add canonical function-call prompt suite to CI and enable parallel runs for fp8/int8/float
Expose alerts in Console and add canary rollback automation for Dedicated/private rollouts
Write runbook and postmortem template for schema-degradation incidents
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Spike completed — prototype per-field scorer implemented in py (scorer/proto) and validated on 2k archived requests. Observed common failure modes: truncated arrays (45%), enum drift (30%), numeric range errors (15%).

2026-03-12: Design review with PM/Design — agreed to represent field confidence as calibrated probability (Platt scaling on scorer logits) and to include token-provenance tags for repair heuristics. Feedback: product wants top-3 suggested actions surfaced in Console.

2026-03-13: Instrumentation PR opened: github.com/redwood/realtime/pull/1248 — adds structured-output trace export and lightweight sampling for Retro-Calibration jobs. Requesting review from @elaine and @samir.

2026-03-14: First CI run on canonical suite shows composite health delta: fp8 -3.7%, int8 -6.1% vs float baseline on small 500-prompt set. Tagging examples and seeding failing prompts into ticket for triage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-sensitive scoring may trigger false positives and unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: calibrate thresholds using 90-day production traffic and add hysteresis windows before halting rollouts.

Risk: Suggested calibration actions could increase latency or memory. Mitigation: each suggestion includes estimated perf delta and we run a short perf regression test in staging before applying to canary.
Risk: Privacy/regulatory constraints for storing request examples. Mitigation: sample and redact PII, keep raw examples only in customer-owned private deployment buckets when applicable.
Risk: Added CI runtime cost for exhaustive quant profile runs. Mitigation: progressive sampling and nightly full sweep; fast smoke checks on PRs.
